consensus_summary: The blind consensus identifies “the Way” primarily as Jesus Christ himself (the exclusive path to the Father and salvation per John 14:6) together with the early Christian movement and life of discipleship (Acts usage); moral/Torah/eschatological senses appear as secondary or layered alternatives that feed into the christological core.
book_summary: The book defines the term as “Covenant conduct — the walk,” while explicitly noting the common teaching as Jesus Himself as the one way to the Father and the narrow way against the broad; its printed texts are Jer 6:16 (old/good way to walk) and Matt 7:14 (narrow way).
consensus_core_identification: Jesus Christ as the exclusive way/path to God and salvation (with the Christian discipleship that follows him).
book_core_identification: Covenant conduct—the walk (obedience in the good/old/narrow paths).
boundary_disagreement: Consensus places the person of Christ at the center (Acts “Way” and moral path as secondary or fulfilled by him); the book places ethical covenant walking at the center and treats the christological reading as the merely common alternative, thereby excluding Christ-as-referent from the primary identification.
material_contradiction: The consensus primary claim that the Way is Christ himself cannot stand if the term’s core meaning is instead covenant conduct/the walk; the book replaces the christological referent rather than merely narrowing cases around it.
rationale: Minimum cores are non-equivalent: consensus (settled primary across A–C) is the person of Christ as path to the Father, while the book is the ethical walk of covenant obedience. Although the moral-path sense is listed as a common alternative, the book’s entry presents “covenant conduct—the walk” as its definition and flags the christological reading as the distinct common view; this is replacement of the central referent, not boundary refinement of the same referent. Partial extension overlap exists on Matt 7:14’s narrow way, but the cores remain incompatible in the same sense.
strongest_objection: The dominant NT symbolic identification (John 14:6 + Acts “the Way”) is christological; redefining the term as covenant conduct subordinates or displaces that settled core without textual warrant in the printed entry itself.
